company.name: Abridge
company.category: Ambient AI documentation and clinician intelligence

products.name: Ambient Documentation
products.desc: Listens to the patient-clinician conversation and drafts structured, specialty-aware notes into the EHR in real time. Supports 28+ languages and 50+ specialties, with Epic Haiku capture and Hyperdrive drafting. Linked Evidence maps generated statements back to source text for auditability.

products.name: Abridge Assistant
products.desc: The AI assistant for healthcare. Clinicians ask questions and delegate tasks in natural language; Assistant pulls context from the chart, the clinical conversation, and licensed evidence (UpToDate, NEJM, JAMA Network, ADA, AAFP, Neurology, JCO), citing sources and opening calculators pre-filled with chart values. Runs inside the EHR and on mobile, under health-system security and governance. As of the September release, every clinician at all 300+ partner health systems has access, whether or not they use Abridge for documentation. Unifies and supersedes the prior Context-Aware Clinical Decision Support and Clinician Intelligence Agent capabilities. August 2026 release added AMA PRA Category 1 CME credits for eligible questions, voice input (Speak to Abridge AI), Voiceprint personalization, medical calculators pre-filled from chart context, pre-visit/pre-admission/pre-round summaries, and inline CPT Level of Service with evidence. September 2026 release added inpatient cues, inline diagnosis organization, expanded specialty support, and admin/CDI controls. October 2026 blog post detailed specialty-aware pre-visit summaries across outpatient, inpatient, and ED settings, with personalization via Abridge Assistant coming in a future release. October 2026 release added Visit Topics (chronic-condition tracking with Medicare Advantage HCC gap detection), In-Visit Orders (orders staged in Epic's Heard in Visit Recording module as discussed), patient visit summary editing via Assistant (reading level, plain language, tone, length), chart-informed inpatient H&P and progress notes citing chart sources inline, outpatient CDI queries and cues via the Query Engine, inpatient diagnosis write-back at note signature, and an Evaluation Dashboard for governance teams. November 2026 added Visit Dx enhancements (diagnosis organization under problem headers, search-and-replace, specificity modifiers) and Local Pathways (institution-specific care guidance surfaced alongside published evidence, with links to source documents). Maine Health and Children's Hospital of Philadelphia cited as using pre-visit summaries. UC Irvine Health and Dayton Children's Hospital cited as Local Pathways design partners.

products.name: Context-Aware Clinical Decision Support
products.desc: Answers clinical questions inside the documentation workflow using the patient conversation plus chart context. Responses are grounded in licensed evidence from UpToDate, NEJM, JAMA Network, ADA, AAFP, Neurology, and JCO, with citations back to source. Runs on Abridge's Contextual Reasoning Engine; patient data is not used for training. Unified under Abridge Assistant as of October 2026.

products.name: Clinician Intelligence Agent
products.desc: Extended context-aware decision support to every clinician at a partner health system, regardless of how they document. Delivered through the existing EHR workflow or a new mobile and web app. Unified under Abridge Assistant as of October 2026.

products.name: Pre-Bill Review
products.desc: First mid-revenue-cycle product. Reconciles coded diagnoses and DRGs against the documented clinical conversation before claim submission, giving CDI, coding, and revenue cycle teams an evidence trail for inpatient claims. Targets documentation-integrity denials and rework.

products.name: Revenue Cycle & Prior Authorization
products.desc: Coding, CDI, and payer connectivity built on the same conversation data model. The Availity collaboration connects Abridge documentation to AI-assisted prior authorization and payer adjudication. Eli Lilly and health-system partners are the anchor design customers for downstream payment workflows.

products.name: Life Sciences / Trial Screening
products.desc: Uses the clinical conversation to surface potential clinical-trial eligibility and screening pathways at the point of care. Eli Lilly made a strategic investment and is the marquee partner; Abridge frames the module as connecting care delivery to research access without a separate screening app.

products.name: Ambient AI for Nursing
products.desc: Captures conversational care and converts it into EHR flowsheets for nursing documentation. KLAS awarded a 94.3 early performance score, citing reduced nursing workflow burden and more complete charting. Expands Abridge beyond physician notes into team-based documentation.

products.name: Abridge Inside for Inpatient
products.desc: Inpatient deployment model with UPMC committed to scale Abridge to 12,000+ clinicians across 40+ hospitals. Extends the ambulatory-first product into hospital medicine, where note complexity and DRG linkage are higher.

products.name: Clinical-Conversation Foundation Model (with NVIDIA)
products.desc: Abridge and NVIDIA are co-developing a foundation model trained on de-identified clinical conversations using the NVIDIA Nemotron family, rather than adapting a general-purpose LLM. The model is expected to launch later in 2026 and run exclusively inside Abridge's platform for documentation and decision support.

products.name: Care Signals
products.desc: Co-developed with Kaiser Permanente over 15 months. Before the visit, Care Signals surfaces a patient's most relevant chronic conditions and care gaps as cue cards. During the visit, it tracks whether each condition is discussed and prompts the clinician if an assessment and plan are absent. After the visit, it produces ICD-10 codes and industry-standard documentation. Moves HCC capture and CDI into the exam room rather than retrospectively.

products.name: Epic Integration / Abridge Inside
products.desc: Abridge was the first Pal in Epic's Partners and Pals program. Capture runs in Epic Haiku, drafting in Hyperdrive, with co-development through Epic Workshop. The depth of this integration is both Abridge's strongest distribution moat and its largest strategic risk as Epic builds native AI charting.

research.title: KLAS Ambient AI 2026: A High-Performing Market Shifts
research.finding: Abridge, Ambience, and Suki lead on innovation as broader capabilities become table stakes. KLAS reports that Abridge leads in buying decisions as EHR-native competitors enter the category.
research.caveat: KLAS scores reflect customer feedback and are not a clinical-outcome trial.

research.title: KLAS First Look: Abridge Ambient AI for Nursing
research.finding: Overall early performance score of 94.3/100. Reviewers cite reduced nursing workflow burden and more complete flowsheet documentation from conversational care capture.
research.caveat: First Look reports are early, small-sample evaluations, not peer-reviewed trials.

research.title: JAMA: Ambient Scribes and EHR Time Across Five Academic Medical Centers
research.finding: AI-powered ambient scribes modestly reduced total EHR time by 13.4 minutes and documentation time by 16.0 minutes per encounter across five academic medical centers.
research.caveat: Multi-vendor study (Ambience, Nuance DAX, others); not Abridge-specific. Effect size is modest relative to total documentation burden.

research.title: JAMA Network Open: Ambient AI Scribes and Physician Burnout
research.finding: Among 263 physicians across six U.S. health systems, ambient AI scribe use was associated with a dramatic reduction in burnout after one month. Benefits clustered around cognitive burden and after-hours documentation.
research.caveat: Quality-improvement design without randomization; self-reported burnout outcomes.

research.title: NEJM AI: Pragmatic Randomized Trial of Ambient AI and Clinician Well-Being
research.finding: A pragmatic RCT at a large academic health system tested ambient AI documentation against usual care for health-practitioner well-being. The Abridge team provided technical support and manuscript review.
research.caveat: Single-system trial; well-being endpoints rather than note accuracy or patient outcomes.

research.title: JAMIA: Clinician Interviews on an Ambient AI Documentation Platform
research.finding: Clinicians reported decreased cognitive burden and singled out Abridge's handling of non-English visits and the History of Present Illness / Patient Instructions sections as differentiated strengths.
research.caveat: Qualitative interview sample; vendor-specific experience may not generalize.

research.title: Comparative Study of Three Ambient Listening Systems
research.finding: A three-system comparison of ambient listening tools examined documentation quality, edit burden, and clinician experience. Added to the OpenEvidence research index during the Oct 17 weekly sweep.
research.caveat: Small comparative sample; product versions change quickly.

research.title: Abridge: Evaluating AI-Generated Documentation and Hallucinations
research.finding: Describes Abridge's evaluation process for generated documentation, quantitative performance measures for key systems, and clinician-in-the-loop studies focused on hallucination detection and linked evidence.
research.caveat: Vendor-authored. Methodology is disclosed but results are not independently replicated.

research.title: Business Insider: Inside the Abridge-Epic Relationship
research.finding: Epic, once an Abridge partner and shareholder, is now building native AI charting that competes directly with third-party scribes. Abridge told hospital customers its integrations would remain intact.
research.caveat: Reporting based on unnamed insiders; strategic risk, not a product evaluation.

timeline.title: Abridge and NACHC Make Abridge Assistant Available to 108,000 Community Health Center Clinicians
timeline.desc: Abridge and the National Association of Community Health Centers (NACHC) announced the Abridge Assistant will be available at no cost to 108,000 clinicians at all NACHC member community health centers, serving approximately 52 million patients — nearly one in seven Americans and one in three rural residents. Clinicians can use the Assistant for clinical decision support with cited evidence regardless of whether they use Abridge's documentation product. CEO Shiv Rao framed it as expanding access and equity through AI. NACHC's Sean Roddy cited the partnership's potential to put practical AI tools within reach of more community health center clinicians.

timeline.title: Abridge Assistant Adds Local Pathways: Health System Care Guidance at the Point of Care
timeline.desc: Abridge announced support for local pathways within the Abridge Assistant, surfacing a health system's own preferred care plans alongside published medical literature. When an applicable institutional pathway is found, the Assistant shows the relevant content with a link to the original source for clinician review. Dr. Shiv Rao framed the goal as turning standards of care into more consistent care at the moment of decision. Dr. Deepti Pandita (UC Irvine Health) and Dr. Abiodun Omoloja (Dayton Children's) endorsed the workflow-integrated approach. The capability runs on existing Abridge enterprise infrastructure that has already passed each institution's security review.

timeline.title: Abridge Visit Dx Enhancements: Organize, Search, and Refine Diagnoses in the Note
timeline.desc: Abridge released Visit Dx enhancements giving clinicians more control over diagnoses in the generated note. New capabilities include organizing diagnoses under problem headers so the assessment reads the way clinicians think, searching and replacing diagnoses without leaving the note, and refining diagnoses with specificity modifiers like laterality and acuity. The update continues Abridge's push to make the AI-generated note editable and clinically precise at the point of care rather than requiring post-visit cleanup.

timeline.title: KLAS Ambient AI 2026: High-Performing Market Shifts as EHR-Native Tools Compress Standalone Scribes
timeline.desc: KLAS Research's October 2026 Ambient AI market report finds the category remains one of healthcare IT's highest-performing markets, but average satisfaction scores have slipped as EHR-native tools raise expectations and compress pricing. The report identifies three market shifts: native EHR ambient tools gaining share, health systems renegotiating contracts, and standalone vendors differentiating on adjacent capabilities like CDI and decision support. Abridge remains the top-ranked vendor at 94.7.

timeline.title: Machine.net: Abridge and Heidi Health Cut Staff Within Days as Hospital Sales Lag
timeline.desc: Machine.net reports that Abridge (valued at $5.3B) and Heidi Health (Australian rival valued at A$1.26B) both cut staff within days of each other, signaling a consolidation phase in the ambient AI scribe market. The analysis ties the dual layoffs to Epic native AI charting tool compressing the standalone scribe market, with hospital procurement cycles slowing as EHR-bundled alternatives reduce willingness to pay for third-party tools. The piece frames this as the most crowded corner of healthcare AI entering a shakeout.

timeline.title: Refolk: Abridge and Heidi Health Both Cut Staff in the Same Week
timeline.desc: Refolk reports that Heidi Health, an Australian ambient AI scribe competitor, also cut staff in the same week as Abridge's layoffs. The analysis notes health systems employ approximately 4.8 analysts per vendor implementation seat, and frames the dual cuts as a signal that the ambient AI vendor market is consolidating as EHR-native tools compress pricing. The article provides transition guidance for displaced implementation and engineering staff moving from vendors to health systems.

timeline.title: Pittsburgh Business Times: Abridge Layoffs Hit Founding City, Local Impact Undisclosed
timeline.desc: Pittsburgh Business Times reports that Abridge, founded in Pittsburgh, laid off an undisclosed number of employees. The article notes the startup raised hundreds of millions in venture capital but has largely scaled elsewhere, and impacts to its Pittsburgh footprint were not disclosed. The local coverage adds geographic context to the company-wide realignment first reported by Modern Healthcare.

timeline.title: Yale Students Raise Privacy and Accuracy Concerns About Abridge at Yale Health
timeline.desc: Yale Daily News reports that Yale Health incorporated Abridge in 2024 to draft notes from patient-provider conversations. Two years in, students express varying levels of comfort with the technology, citing concerns about privacy and accuracy of AI-generated documentation. The article highlights patient-side acceptance as a continuing adoption risk for ambient AI, even as clinician adoption accelerates. Yale Health is a campus health clinic distinct from Yale New Haven Health System, which is a separate Abridge enterprise customer.

timeline.title: Refolk Analysis: Abridge Layoffs Targeted Speech and LLM-Evaluation Engineers
timeline.desc: A technical hiring analysis by Refolk finds that Abridge's November layoffs affected speech recognition and LLM-evaluation engineers, based on job-board diffs and office geography. The report notes the headcount cut may never trigger a WARN notice due to its size, and identifies 19 engineering requisitions that were removed. The analysis suggests Abridge is trimming specialized AI talent as the market shifts from model-building to product integration.

timeline.title: Abridge VP Dr. Nadim Ilbawi on Becker's Podcast: Context-Aware Clinical Decision Support
timeline.desc: Dr. Nadim Ilbawi, VP of Clinical Success & Strategy at Abridge, appeared on Becker's Healthcare Podcast to discuss how AI-powered clinical decision support brings patient chart information and trusted medical evidence together. The conversation covers how Abridge Assistant helps clinicians prepare for visits, make informed decisions during encounters, and reduce cognitive burden by grounding responses in the patient conversation and licensed evidence sources.

timeline.title: Abridge Lays Off Employees in Company Realignment
timeline.desc: Modern Healthcare reports Abridge has laid off an unspecified number of employees as part of a company realignment. Abridge said the move will allow it to hire in priority areas and invest in new opportunities. No headcount, department, or percentage was disclosed. The layoff signals a shift in the ambient AI market from land-grab growth toward margin discipline as EHR-native competitors and model platforms pressure pricing.

timeline.title: Lawsuit Filed Against AHN and Highmark Over Abridge AI Recording
timeline.desc: A Pittsburgh-area woman filed a class-action lawsuit in Allegheny County Common Pleas Court against Allegheny Health Network and Highmark, alleging improper disclosure and use of Abridge's AI recording tool during patient visits. The suit claims patients were not properly informed that their conversations would be recorded, transmitted to Abridge servers, and potentially used for commercial AI training. It cites Pennsylvania wiretap law, HIPAA, breach of confidentiality, and invasion of privacy. AHN has deployed Abridge across approximately 400 providers in 40+ specialties since 2024. Similar lawsuits have been filed in California.

timeline.title: Abridge Launches Assistant Prompt Library with 300+ Curated Prompts
timeline.desc: Abridge introduced the Assistant Prompt Library, a growing collection of 300+ curated prompts organized by specialty and use case - chart prep, chart query, clinical decision support, note editing, and generating new artifacts. The library offers a window into how clinicians are putting Abridge Assistant into practice and is browseable on the Abridge website. Abridge called Assistant the fastest-growing product in its history.

timeline.title: Abridge Carries $6.69B Private Valuation as Independent Trials Measure 22-Minute Daily Savings
timeline.desc: The Inference reports Abridge's latest private valuation mark at $6.69 billion, up from the $5.3B set in June 2025. The article cites independent trial evidence - a 24-week RCT across 66 practitioners finding 0.36 hours/day note-time reduction, a UCLA head-to-head in NEJM AI, and a VHA evaluation where human note-takers outscored 11 AI scribes - as the first countable productivity metric (22 minutes/day) that caps per-encounter pricing and shifts margin to clinical content and mid-revenue-cycle workflow.

timeline.title: Becker's: Abridge Pushes CDI Closer to Care with Concurrent Queries and Pre-Bill Review
timeline.desc: Becker's Hospital Review published a field report on how Abridge is moving clinical documentation integrity from a retrospective function into the encounter itself. Concurrent CDI surfaces documentation gaps while clinicians write notes during hospital stays; pre-bill review compares coded diagnoses and DRGs against the documented conversation before the claim drops. The article frames this as Abridge pushing clinical context into adjacent business processes rather than adding more alerts.

timeline.title: Abridge Launches Inpatient Suite for Care Teams and Revenue Cycle
timeline.desc: Abridge VP Product Janie Lee announced the launch of an Inpatient Suite designed for the complexity of inpatient care - spanning days, shifts, and handoffs with many clinicians contributing to one patient record. The suite helps clinicians walk into admissions and rounds fully oriented, creates notes that follow the patient's stay, and supports CDI and billing along the way. Documentation gaps are addressed at the point of care rather than retrospectively.

timeline.title: Abridge October 2026 Release: Visit Topics, In-Visit Orders, Chart-Informed Inpatient Notes, Outpatient CDI, Evaluation Dashboard
timeline.desc: Abridge's October 'Now in Practice' release adds Visit Topics (chronic-condition tracking with Medicare Advantage HCC gap detection), In-Visit Orders (orders staged in Epic as they are discussed), patient visit summary editing via Abridge Assistant, chart-informed inpatient H&P and progress notes that cite chart sources inline, outpatient CDI queries and cues through the Query Engine, inpatient diagnosis write-back to the chart at note signature, and an Evaluation Dashboard giving governance teams transparency into how Abridge's clinical AI is measured. The release moves more CDI and order-capture work into the encounter itself.

timeline.title: Maine Health Case Study: Abridge Assistant in Family Medicine Practice
timeline.desc: Abridge published a case study with Dr. Jessica Faraci, a family medicine physician at Maine Health, describing how she uses Abridge Assistant for in-visit decision support, generating patient summaries, writing medical letters, and creating patient handouts. Faraci reports Assistant saves roughly 30 minutes per day on top of documentation time savings, with about half of its auto-generated clinical questions matching what she was already thinking. The case study is the first public confirmation that Maine Health is an Abridge enterprise partner.

timeline.title: Abridge Details Pre-Visit Summaries: Specialty-Aware, Setting-Specific, Coming Personalization
timeline.desc: Abridge published an in-depth blog post on how pre-visit summaries are built and evaluated across outpatient, inpatient, and emergency settings. The summaries filter the EHR problem list by specialty, surface relevant changes since the last visit, and are now available across 300+ health systems. An upcoming release will let clinicians personalize summaries through Abridge Assistant in real time. Clinicians at Akron Children's Hospital and Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) are cited as using the feature.

timeline.title: Suki Raises $90M Series E to Build AI Agents for Referrals and Prior Auths
timeline.desc: Suki, Abridge's closest ambient AI competitor, closed a $90M Series E led by Healthier Capital, bringing total raised to $250M+. The funding will push Suki beyond clinical notes into AI agents that autonomously draft referrals, submit prior authorizations, place orders, and schedule follow-ups - directly competing with Abridge's Availity prior-auth partnership and revenue cycle expansion. Suki reports 450+ organizations, 30+ technology partners, and 190% YoY encounter growth.

timeline.title: Deaconess Health: Abridge Assistant in Psychiatric Practice (Olivia Taylor Case Study)
timeline.desc: Abridge published a case study with Olivia Taylor, a psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner at Deaconess Health with a decade of experience across inpatient and outpatient care. Taylor describes using Abridge Assistant for context-aware decision support during visits, including verifying medication taper strategies, monitoring schedules, and drug interactions - without leaving the conversation. She reports it has given her back significant mental bandwidth and sharpened her critical thinking by surfacing angles she hadn't considered. The case study confirms Deaconess Health as an Abridge enterprise partner with unlimited clinician licenses.

timeline.title: Abridge September 2026 Release: Inpatient Cues, New Specialty Support, Admin Controls
timeline.desc: Abridge's September 'Now in Practice' release adds inpatient cues that capture observations from the bedside while the story is still fresh, inline diagnosis organization and refinement (so combination codes surface before the chart closes), expanded specialty support, and two new admin controls giving project and CDI teams direct control over access management and output verification. The release closes the gap between care delivered and care documented at the point of care.

timeline.title: Abridge Launches Abridge Assistant, the AI Assistant for Healthcare
timeline.desc: Abridge introduced Abridge Assistant, a conversational AI assistant that lets clinicians ask questions and delegate tasks in natural language. Assistant pulls context from the patient chart, the clinical conversation, and trusted evidence sources (UpToDate, NEJM, JAMA, ADA, AAFP, Neurology, JCO), with every response citing its sources and opening calculators pre-filled with chart values. As of the September release, every clinician at all 300+ partner health systems has access, whether or not they use Abridge for documentation. The launch unifies the prior Context-Aware Clinical Decision Support and Clinician Intelligence Agent capabilities under a single brand.

timeline.title: Corewell Health Deploys Abridge Assistant in Primary Care
timeline.desc: Corewell Health, Michigan's largest health system (21 hospitals, 300+ outpatient locations), is using Abridge Assistant in clinical practice. Dr. Kristin Jacob, an internal medicine-pediatrics clinician and Medical Director of Physician and APP Well-Being, described using Assistant for pre-charting, in-visit decision support, and patient messages - cutting Sunday chart prep from roughly two hours to minutes and enabling in-the-moment patient education. The case study is the first public confirmation that Corewell Health is an Abridge enterprise customer.

timeline.title: Abridge Launches Physician Builder Challenge with OpenAI at HLTH 2026
timeline.desc: Abridge announced the Physician Builder Challenge in partnership with Physician Side Gigs and OpenAI, inviting physicians attending HLTH 2026 to pitch solutions to practical healthcare challenges. Three selected ideas will be developed into working prototypes with Abridge's team and showcased at the Physicians at HLTH reception on November 16. Submissions closed October 20. The initiative marks Abridge's first public collaboration with OpenAI and positions the platform as a co-development environment for clinician-driven innovation.

timeline.title: University of Texas System Goes Enterprise-Wide with Abridge
timeline.desc: Abridge announced an enterprise-wide agreement with UT REAL Health AI covering the eight University of Texas health institutions. The framework lets each institution adopt Abridge on its own timeline while preserving local decision-making. It builds on a year-long pilot that expanded significantly across UT clinicians and follows the VA enterprise win two weeks earlier.

timeline.title: WashU Medicine and BJC Health Expand Abridge to 4,000 Clinicians
timeline.desc: The Center for Health AI at WashU Medicine and BJC Health expanded Abridge across BJC's East Region after a rigorous pilot evaluation. Documentation time fell 8% initially, rising to 15% by day 150; after-hours documentation dropped 6% initially, reaching 20% reduction by day 150. Outpatient specialties including family medicine, internal medicine, OB/GYN, pediatrics, and orthopedic surgery saw particularly strong adoption.

timeline.title: Abridge Wins Seat on $775.7M VA Ambient AI Enterprise Contract
timeline.desc: The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs selected Abridge, through a distribution partner, for a five-year multi-award enterprise contract with a collective ceiling of $775.72 million. The vehicle lets VA medical centers and regions bring ambient AI to clinicians serving 9M+ veterans, across both VistA/CPRS and the Federal EHR. Knowtex also holds a seat and will compete for task orders.

timeline.title: WVU Medicine: Abridge Assistant in Emergency Medicine (Dr. Brian Dilcher Case Study)
timeline.desc: Abridge published a case study with Dr. Brian Dilcher, an emergency medicine physician and associate CMIO for emergency medicine at WVU Medicine's Ruby Memorial Hospital, a Level I trauma center. Dilcher describes using Abridge's context-aware clinical intelligence to spot-check decisions against evidence in the fast-paced ED environment, surface patterns from prior visits that would otherwise be missed in the noise, and verify medication and treatment approaches in natural language without leaving the workflow. He cites repeatability, consistency, and source transparency as the reasons he endorsed it to colleagues and residents.

timeline.title: Abridge Enters the Mid-Revenue Cycle with Pre-Bill Review
timeline.desc: Abridge launched a pre-bill review capability for clinical documentation integrity (CDI), coding, and revenue cycle teams. It audits inpatient claims and DRGs against the bedside clinical conversation before the claim drops, surfacing discrepancies between coded diagnoses and documented evidence. First product built specifically for the mid-revenue cycle.

timeline.title: Abridge August 2026 Release: CME Credits, Pre-Visit Summaries, Voiceprints
timeline.desc: Abridge's August 'Now in Practice' release introduced eight capabilities built on context Abridge already has. Clinicians can now claim AMA PRA Category 1 credit for eligible Abridge AI questions, use medical calculators pre-filled from chart context, speak to Abridge AI instead of typing, enroll a Voiceprint for personalized speech recognition, and access pre-visit, pre-admission, and pre-round summaries. Inline Level of Service places CPT code evidence directly below Assessment & Plan.

timeline.title: Abridge Named a Fast Company Most Innovative Company of 2026
timeline.desc: Fast Company recognized Abridge for changing how healthcare works for providers, patients, and payers. The honor adds to a wall that already includes Best in KLAS for Ambient AI in 2025 and 2026, TIME Best Inventions, and CNBC Disruptor 50.

timeline.title: Sutter Health + Abridge: Building and Scaling Clinical AI Together
timeline.desc: Abridge published a detailed partnership timeline with Sutter Health, which first piloted Abridge in 2024. Sutter Health serves 3.6 million patients with approximately 64,000 clinicians, staff, and affiliated physicians, and has scaled one of the widest and deepest enterprise AI deployments in U.S. healthcare. The blog post traces the evolution from pilot to system-wide adoption across ambulatory and inpatient settings.

timeline.title: Context-Aware Clinical Intelligence Opened to Every Clinician at Partner Systems
timeline.desc: Abridge now lets partner health systems extend its clinical intelligence agent to every clinician, regardless of how that clinician documents visits today. Access can run through the EHR workflow clinicians already use or through a new mobile and web experience, each connected to the patient chart. More than 300 enterprise health systems representing over 250 million patients adopted the decision support since its April launch.

timeline.title: Deaconess Health Expands Abridge to Unlimited Enterprise License After Clinician Demand
timeline.desc: Deaconess Health System, an Indiana-based system, expanded Abridge from a 200-license pilot to an unlimited enterprise-wide agreement after clinician demand outpaced every license tier set by leadership. Adoption spread by word-of-mouth across specialties, with locum clinicians citing Abridge as a reason to choose Deaconess over other opportunities. The system moved to an unlimited model and is now piloting Abridge for nursing and extending access to non-Deaconess-employed clinicians. First public confirmation that Deaconess Health is an Abridge enterprise partner.

timeline.title: Abridge and Kaiser Permanente Debut Care Signals
timeline.desc: Care Signals is a new capability co-designed with Kaiser Permanente over 15 months. Before a visit, it flags a patient's most relevant chronic conditions and care gaps. During the visit, it tracks whether each condition is discussed and cues the clinician if an assessment and plan are missing. After the visit, it generates ICD-10 codes and documentation that match. The tool moves CDI and HCC capture into the visit itself rather than weeks later.

timeline.title: Abridge Unveils AI-Native Clinician Intelligence Platform
timeline.desc: At a New York keynote, Abridge introduced a platform that extends from documentation into billing, clinical decision support, payer adjudication, and pharmaceutical trial screening. The company announced a collaboration with NVIDIA on the first foundation model purpose-built for clinical conversations, a strategic investment from Eli Lilly, partnerships with Artisight and Hellocare, and content deals with ADA, AAFP, Neurology, and JCO. Northwestern Medicine was named as an enterprise rollout.

timeline.title: Abridge Named to CNBC Disruptor 50 List for Second Year
timeline.desc: CNBC named Abridge to its 2026 Disruptor 50 list at No. 30, up from No. 47 in 2025. The recognition cites $550M raised across Series D and E rounds, expansion into clinical decision support and peer-reviewed research, and a $5.3B valuation. Abridge was one of few healthcare AI companies on the list.

timeline.title: Abridge Names San Oo Chief Technology Officer
timeline.desc: Abridge appointed San Oo as CTO. Oo was most recently SVP of Engineering at Notion and previously co-founded two companies acquired by LinkedIn and Slack. CEO Shiv Rao cited Oo's track record of platform-level rethinks that alter the texture of work. Oo joins at an inflection point as Abridge scales from documentation into a real-time system of intelligence across 270+ health systems.

timeline.title: Abridge Summit at Becker's: Health Systems Operationalize Real-Time Intelligence
timeline.desc: A field report from the Abridge summit at Becker's 16th Annual Meeting reveals OhioHealth (16-hospital system) and UI Health as Abridge enterprise customers. Reid Health's CDIO described Abridge as the 'wiring' of the health system, reporting a 6% lift in patient-experience scores, 4% increase in wRVUs, improved HCC capture, fewer CDI queries, and a drop in outpatient denials. Northwestern Medicine and Sutter Health leaders discussed conversation-driven clinical decision support and the shift from documentation tool to system of intelligence.

timeline.title: CHRISTUS Health Expands to Unlimited Enterprise Agreement, Adds Inpatient and Nursing
timeline.desc: CHRISTUS Health, a 60+ hospital system across the U.S. and Mexico, expanded its Abridge partnership from ambulatory care to an unlimited enterprise agreement while introducing AI into inpatient care and launching a pilot for nursing documentation. Dr. Tim Barker, System Medical Director and CMIO of Ambulatory Care, cited continuous innovation and trust built over several years of ambulatory success as the driver for expansion.

timeline.title: HonorHealth Skips Pilot, Goes Enterprise-Wide with Abridge
timeline.desc: HonorHealth, a Scottsdale, AZ health system serving 5M+ patients annually across 9 acute-care hospitals and 200+ care locations, selected Abridge after a three-and-a-half-year search and skipped the pilot phase entirely. The enterprise-wide rollout began January 2026 with 500 clinicians across ambulatory and inpatient settings using a wave-based deployment strategy. CMIO Dr. Matthew Anderson said clinicians who initially rejected ambient AI were asking for it within weeks.

timeline.title: Abridge Adds NEJM Group and JAMA Network Evidence to Clinical Decision Support
timeline.desc: Multi-year content partnerships bring NEJM and the JAMA Network (JAMA plus 11 specialty journals and JAMA Network Open) into Abridge's clinical decision support. The tool already surfaces context-aware insights from Wolters Kluwer's UpToDate. The same journal partners anchor OpenEvidence's evidence library, marking direct convergence between the two platforms.

timeline.title: KLAS First Look Scores Abridge Ambient AI for Nursing at 94.3
timeline.desc: KLAS Research's First Look report on Abridge Ambient AI for Nursing awarded an overall early performance score of 94.3 out of 100. The product converts conversational care into EHR flowsheets, targeting nursing documentation burden and incomplete charting. It extends Abridge from physician documentation into nursing workflows.

timeline.title: Abridge Raises $316M Series E Extension at $5.3B
timeline.desc: Abridge closed a reported $316M extension to its Series E at the same $5.3B valuation set in June 2025. Reported total capital raised now ranges from roughly $830M to $1.07B depending on how the extension and earlier rounds are counted. The flat price, ten months after the prior mark, signals scale-up execution rather than a fresh valuation step-up.

timeline.title: University Hospitals Selects Abridge as Strategic Enterprise Partner After Head-to-Head Evaluation
timeline.desc: University Hospitals, a Cleveland-based academic health system, selected Abridge as its long-term enterprise AI partner after a rigorous head-to-head vendor evaluation including crossover clinicians, formal scorecards, and executive reviews. Every crossover user preferred Abridge, citing note quality and workflow fit. The selection adds another major academic medical center to Abridge's enterprise roster.

timeline.title: Forbes Names Shiv Rao to Inaugural 250 Greatest Living Innovators List
timeline.desc: Forbes named Abridge Founder and CEO Shiv Rao, MD, to its inaugural list of America's 250 Greatest Living Innovators. The list was compiled with input from Forbes beat reporters, a panel of judges including Jim Breyer and Kara Swisher, and AI-assisted ranking. The recognition places Rao alongside figures like Elon Musk, Jennifer Doudna, and Sam Altman.

timeline.title: UCHealth Rapidly Expands Abridge AI Across 2,300+ Providers
timeline.desc: UCHealth, a Colorado-based nonprofit health system, partnered with Abridge to bring enterprise-grade AI across the state. The decision follows a successful nine-month pilot with 250 UCHealth providers in 2025 that demonstrated significant improvements in patient experience and provider workflows. Over one-third of about 6,000 UCHealth doctors now have access to Abridge.

timeline.title: Abridge Wins #1 Best in KLAS 2026 for Ambient AI, Second Year Running
timeline.desc: Abridge earned the No. 1 Best in KLAS 2026 ranking for Ambient AI in the Revenue Cycle Management category for the second consecutive year. The ranking is based on independent customer interviews with large enterprise health systems, not vendor-submitted data. KLAS's 2026 Ambient AI report also placed Abridge among the innovation leaders and said it leads buying decisions.

timeline.title: Epic Launches Built-In AI Charting Tool, Intensifying Competition with Ambient Scribe Vendors
timeline.desc: Epic rolled out a native AI charting tool that listens during appointments, drafts clinical documentation, and prepares orders based on what it hears. With 42% of the acute care EHR market, Epic's entry puts it in direct competition with third-party ambient AI scribes like Abridge, which relies on deep Epic integration as a distribution moat. The move raises questions about how long standalone scribes can maintain privileged access to Epic workflows.

timeline.title: Abridge and Availity Partner on AI-Powered Prior Authorization
timeline.desc: Abridge partnered with Availity to connect clinical documentation to payer workflows and AI-assisted prior authorization. The collaboration pushes Abridge downstream from the note into payment adjudication, one of the most friction-heavy steps between visit and reimbursement.

timeline.title: Inova Health Selects Abridge as System-Wide Generative AI Platform
timeline.desc: Inova Health, a Northern Virginia health system, chose Abridge as its system-wide generative AI platform for clinical conversations. The Abridge AI platform converts patient-clinician conversations into clinical notes for Inova's healthcare providers, aiming to improve documentation quality and clinician experience.

timeline.title: Seattle Children's Deploys Abridge Enterprise-Wide
timeline.desc: Seattle Children's implemented Abridge's AI platform across the pediatric health system. The deployment added a major pediatric academic center to an enterprise roster already anchored by Kaiser Permanente, Mayo Clinic, Johns Hopkins, Duke, Emory, Yale New Haven, Sutter, and UPMC.

timeline.title: Epic's Own AI Strategy Turns Its Closest Partner Into Its Biggest Threat
timeline.desc: Business Insider reported growing tension between Abridge and Epic, which was both an early partner and a former shareholder. Epic's native AI charting ambitions raised questions about how long third-party scribes can rely on deep Epic integration as a moat. Abridge told hospital customers its software would remain integrated with Epic.

timeline.title: Series E: $300M at $5.3B Led by a16z
timeline.desc: Andreessen Horowitz led a $300M Series E with Khosla Ventures, nearly doubling Abridge's valuation from $2.75B four months earlier. The company said it was live at more than 150 enterprise health systems and had reached $117M in contracted annual recurring revenue in Q1 2025. Capital was earmarked for new products and revenue-cycle AI.

timeline.title: Series D: $250M at $2.75B
timeline.desc: Abridge raised $250M led by Elad Gil at a $2.75B valuation, with participation from Lightspeed, CVS Health Ventures, and others. The round funded expansion from ambulatory documentation into inpatient and specialty workflows. Fortune profiled CEO Shiv Rao alongside the raise.

timeline.title: Series C: $150M at $850M Valuation
timeline.desc: Abridge raised $150M in a Series C that valued the company at $850M. The round marked the inflection from pilot programs to enterprise deployments across major health systems and set the base for a 6.2x valuation increase over the following two years.

timeline.title: Abridge Founded in Pittsburgh
timeline.desc: Cardiologist Shiv Rao co-founded Abridge with Sandeep Konam and Florian Metze, spinning out of the Pittsburgh Health Data Alliance (UPMC, Carnegie Mellon, University of Pittsburgh). The original thesis: turn the patient-clinician conversation into structured, clinically useful documentation.
